name.text: Digital Logic - Q1: Binary to BCD

questiontext.text:
Convert the following binary number {@bin_str@} to its 8421 BCD equivalent.

BCD = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

Note: Enter the BCD digits separated by spaces, and use a period for the decimal point if applicable (e.g., 0001 0010.0101).

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Step 1: Convert binary to decimal

\[ {@bin_str@}_2 = {@dec_val@}_{10} \]

Step 2: Convert each decimal digit to 4-bit BCD

The decimal digits are {@dec_digits@}.

  • {@dec_digits[1]@} → {@bcd_parts[1]@}
  • {@dec_digits[2]@} → {@bcd_parts[2]@}
  • {@dec_digits[3]@} → {@bcd_parts[3]@}
  • . → .
  • {@dec_frac_digits[1]@} → {@bcd_frac_parts[1]@}
  • {@dec_frac_digits[2]@} → {@bcd_frac_parts[2]@}

BCD equivalent: {@ta1@}

name.text: Digital Logic - Q2: 16-bit Register to Decimal

questiontext.text:
A 16-bit register contains the following BCD contents: {@reg_str@}

Interpret the contents of this register as a decimal number.

Decimal = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Divide the 16-bit content into 4-bit nibbles and convert each to its decimal equivalent:

  • {@bcd_parts[1]@} → {@d1@}
  • {@bcd_parts[2]@} → {@d2@}
  • {@bcd_parts[3]@} → {@d3@}
  • {@bcd_parts[4]@} → {@d4@}

The decimal equivalent is {@ta1@}.

name.text: Digital Logic - Q3: Decimal to Excess-3

questiontext.text:
Express the decimal number {@dec_val@} in excess-3 code.

Excess-3 = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

Note: Enter the 4-bit codes separated by spaces (e.g., 1000 0101).

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To convert to excess-3, add 3 to each decimal digit and find the BCD equivalent of the result:

  • Digit 1: {@d1@} + 3 = {@d1+3@} → {@bcd_map[d1+3+1]@}
  • Digit 2: {@d2@} + 3 = {@d2+3@} → {@bcd_map[d2+3+1]@}
  • Digit 3: {@d3@} + 3 = {@d3+3@} → {@bcd_map[d3+3+1]@}
  • Digit 4: {@d4@} + 3 = {@d4+3@} → {@bcd_map[d4+3+1]@}

Excess-3 code: {@ta1@}

name.text: Digital Logic - Q4: Decimal to Gray Code

questiontext.text:
Determine the 4-bit Gray code for decimal {@dec_val@}.

Gray Code = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Step 1: Convert decimal to binary

\( {@dec_val@}_{10} = {@bin_str@}_2 \)

Step 2: Convert binary to Gray code

Rules: \( g_3 = b_3 \), \( g_2 = b_3 \oplus b_2 \), \( g_1 = b_2 \oplus b_1 \), \( g_0 = b_1 \oplus b_0 \)

Binary: {@b3@} {@b2@} {@b1@} {@b0@}

  • \( g_3 = {@b3@} = {@g3@} \)
  • \( g_2 = {@b3@} \oplus {@b2@} = {@g2@} \)
  • \( g_1 = {@b2@} \oplus {@b1@} = {@g1@} \)
  • \( g_0 = {@b1@} \oplus {@b0@} = {@g0@} \)

Gray code: {@ta1@}
